title: In vivo trunk driving-point stiffness at T12 vs steady-state effort (20/40% max) and horizontal loading direction, standing, pelvis fixed (ACTIVE muscle)
condition: standing, pelvis immobilised, steady-state horizontal effort 20 or 40% of max extension (ACTIVE muscle)

quantity.name: trunk driving-point stiffness k (and effective mass m)
quantity.definition: m d'' + k d = A sin(wt) fitted to the displacement of the harness (load point) during the first half-period of a single sine-wave force perturbation (~253 ms period); damping and gravity neglected; stiffness includes chest soft tissue, harness and frame compliance (likely underestimated)

source.sample: 14 young healthy subjects (8 M, 6 F), 8 with complete data; 726 of 840 trials valid; age 25.7 (3.9) y (20.7-33.2), height 1.76 (0.10) m, mass 73.8 (12.5) kg

protocol.summary: Standing in a braced frame with pads on both ASIS and the sacrum; thoracic harness with cable at ~T12 to a pulley at 0, 45, 90, 135 or 180 deg from anterior (around the right side); subject held a steady horizontal effort (20 or 40% of max extension effort, visual feedback), then a single sine-wave force perturbation of 7.5 or 15% max (28 or 62 N) was superimposed at a random time; displacement by spring-loaded transducer. 3 trials per condition.
how_to_simulate: Standing model with pelvis fixed; apply a horizontal force at T12 in the given direction (0 = pulling anteriorly, i.e. extension effort) of 122 N (20%) or 234 N (40%)
Solve muscle activations to resist the force (include muscle short-range stiffness; reflexes negligible within ~126 ms)

Compute the translational stiffness of the T12 point in the load direction (force increment / displacement increment, or linearised stiffness matrix of the activated system) and compare per direction and effort
protocol.notes: ACTIVE: stiffness from muscle activation at steady effort; never pool with passive tests. Peak trunk displacements 3.8/8.1 mm (20% effort, low/high amplitude) and 2.4/5.7 mm (40%).
